findings.title: Restarted flusher process leaves stale buffer reference and loses the original process on restart
Shared stopped flag and drift across processes, plus join breaks out without terminating the remaining processes
Inconsistent metric tag names and test sleeps

response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Restarted flusher process leaves stale buffer reference and loses the original process on restart

Affected:
- src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:247-259

Explanation:
On restart, `_create_process_for_shards` builds a new `SpansBuffer` and replaces `self.buffers[process_index]`. The old process is only killed if it is a `multiprocessing.Process`. `multiprocessing.Process` is not the class of the objects created from the `spawn` context (`SpawnProcess`). `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` therefore likely returns False, so a hung process is never killed and keeps running next to its replacement. Both then flush the same shards, which causes duplicate flushes. The same wrong check in `join()` means `terminate()` is never called. Fix this by checking against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, or by checking `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
if not isinstance(process, threading.Thread):
    process.kill()
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Shared stopped flag and drift across processes, plus join breaks out without terminating the remaining processes

Affected:
- src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:336-347

Explanation:
When the deadline expires, the loop `break`s and skips `terminate()` for all remaining processes, so they leak. Also, `self.stopped.value = True` is shared by all processes, which is fine. But a process with a short deadline that is not alive still goes through the loop correctly, and the break skips the cleanup for the rest.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
for process in self.processes.values():
    while process.is_alive() and (deadline is None or deadline > time.time()):
        time.sleep(0.1)
    if not isinstance(process, threading.Thread):
        process.terminate()
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Restart-count check and unconditional `max_processes` default

Affected:
- src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:51-60

Explanation:
`max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` is fine. But if `assigned_shards` is empty, `num_processes` is 0 and `i % 0` is never evaluated only because the loop body does not run. Zero processes then silently means no flushing. The default of `flusher_processes=1` in the CLI also changes behavior from before for no stated reason, and may bottleneck consumers that have many shards.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
self.num_processes = max(1, min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards)))
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Inconsistent metric tag names and test sleeps

Affected:
- src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:185-199
- tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:60-62

Explanation:
The tag is `shard` on the produce timer and `shards` on wait_produce, which makes metrics hard to correlate. The test also uses a real `time.sleep(0.1)` after monkeypatching `time.sleep` to a no-op, so the call does nothing and the test remains racy.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
tags={"shard": shard_tag}
~~~

This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
